entities.name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Basilica of Bom Jesus ('Good Jesus') in Old Goa, India, completed in 1605, houses the incorrupt body of St Francis Xavier — one of the founders of the Jesuit order and Asia's most successful Catholic missionary — and is the most visited Christian pilgrimage site in South Asia, receiving 1 million pilgrims during the periodic Exposition of Xavier's body (held every 10-12 years). The basilica is the earliest example of Baroque architecture in India and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, representing the physical legacy of Portuguese colonialism and Jesuit missionary activity across Asia.

Francisco de Xavier (1506-1552), co-founder of the Society of Jesus with Ignatius Loyola, spent his apostolic career (1541-1552) traveling from Goa to India, Sri Lanka, Malacca, the Moluccas, Japan, and China — baptizing an estimated 30,000-700,000 people (numbers vary wildly) in 11 years. He died at Shangchuan Island near China, and his body was brought to Goa in 1554. The body's reported incorruption — preserved without embalming since 1552 — became the basis for Xavier's beatification and the greatest Christian relic in Asia.

The Exposition of Xavier's body, which began in 1782 and occurs every 10-12 years, draws 1 million pilgrims in 45 days. During the 2014 Exposition, 2 million people attended. In the 17th-18th centuries, Portuguese colonial governors carried the body in processions for swearing oaths of office. The basilica's Italian Baroque architecture — the most elaborate church in Portuguese India — represents the Jesuits' use of artistic magnificence as missionary tool: beauty as argument for the Catholic faith.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Basilica of Bom Jesus — housing Francis Xavier's reportedly incorrupt body and drawing millions of pilgrims — is the most significant monument of Catholic missionary activity in Asia, demonstrating the Jesuit use of architectural magnificence and saintly relics as instruments of religious conversion.
